exposure: haemorrhagic complications like bleeding and haematoma
outcome: Incidence of relaparotomy after primary surgery in pregnant women
cohort: Pregnant women who underwent relaparotomy after primary surgery at a tertiary care center
finding: The incidence of relaparotomy was 0.22%, with the most common indication being hemorrhagic complications (66.8%) following cesarean section (94% of cases), and the most common comorbidities being hypertensive disorders (58%) and liver disorders (19%), resulting in a 2.8% maternal mortality rate.
mod_finding: Relaparotomy was most commonly performed after cesarean section (94% of cases).
